title: The trial gyms' shared AI money pool runs out with no warning to MettleUp first
what: All trial and unpaid gyms share one small monthly AI money pool (15 dollars unless changed). Each trial gym may ask 20 questions a day, so a modest number of ordinary trial gyms can use it up before the month ends. Nothing warns MettleUp as the pool fills; when it is used up the server writes one log line and every trial gym is told the AI Assistant is resting till next month. MettleUp learns of it only when an owner complains.
expected: A warning to MettleUp (on HQ Needs you) when the pool passes about 70% and again at 90%, early enough to raise it before trial gyms are turned away.
who: owners of trial gyms, and MettleUp
how_often: any month with more than a handful of active trial gyms
fix_line: Warn MettleUp in HQ as the trial pool fills, and show the pool's level on the System page

title: A paying gym is handled as a trial gym whenever its paid check fails
what: Before each question the server asks whether the gym has paid. If that check cannot be read (gym server slow or down, an odd answer), the paying gym is treated as a trial gym: it gets the smaller 20-a-day allowance, its use is added to the trial gyms' shared money pool, and if that pool is used up it is told the AI Assistant is resting till next month. The owner decided paying gyms are never stopped by a money cap.
expected: A paying gym keeps its own allowance and is never refused by the trial money pool because one check failed; an unreadable check is retried or the last known answer is used.
how_often: when the gym server is slow or down
fix_line: Remember the gym's last known paid answer and use it when the check fails

title: When all gyms together reach the day's speaking ceiling, the owner is told he used up his own time
what: Speaking a request has two daily limits: 10 minutes per gym and 10 hours for all gyms together. Both give the same answer: You have used today's speaking time. An owner who has not spoken at all that day reads that he used his time, when in fact other gyms used the shared ceiling.
expected: At the shared ceiling the owner reads that speaking is busy for today and he can type instead, not that he used his own time.
how_often: on days when many gyms speak requests
fix_line: Tell apart the two limits and give the shared one its own words

title: A spoken request that could not be turned into words still uses up speaking time
what: The clip's seconds are taken from the day's speaking time before the speech service is asked. If every speech service fails, the owner is told to try again or type, but the seconds are not given back. Typed questions that fail are given back; spoken ones are not.
expected: Seconds of a clip that could not be turned into words are given back, as failed typed questions are.
how_often: when the speech service is down
fix_line: Give the seconds back when no speech service answered
